note: Conformance vectors for package schema 3, read by BOTH the Python reader and the browser reader.
They exist because the two readers enforced different contracts while both claiming to read v3.
Python defaulted labels it never counted; the client accepted a null footnote total it then
rendered nowhere, and slot references whose grammar and uniqueness it never checked. A package
could be built, signed and certified on the forge and refused by the browser, and a document the
browser accepted could produce a board that cannot be finished.
Shared DATA, not shared code: forge/ and serve/ still import nothing from each other. Each side
applies these mutations to a real reference package with its own reader, which is what makes the
two implementations answerable to one contract without becoming one implementation.
A vector that both sides accept, or both reject, says nothing on its own. What it forbids is the
two disagreeing.
⚠️ These used to name a package by id, and the first regeneration renamed it — every vector then
failed on a missing reference rather than on anything about the contract. The id is derived from
the game, so it moves whenever the generator's rules change, which is exactly when these matter
most. They run against the manifest's first package now: any published package is a valid subject,
because every mutation below is about the schema rather than about a particular board.
`caps` carries the roster caps §5 and §6 decide. They are a product rule, not a schema field, so no
vector can express them — but the client still has to assert published packages respect them, and
spelling the numbers in a JS test is the twenty-sixth copy of a value that has already outlived one
justification. The definition is forge/src/boxscore_domain, with the reason and the measurement
beside each value; a forge test asserts these two numbers still equal it, so the pair cannot drift
in silence. Shared data, not shared code — the same arrangement as the vectors themselves.

vectors.name: the reference package itself
vectors.because: a guard that rejected everything would satisfy every rejection case below

vectors.name: labels absent
vectors.because: the forge could build, sign and certify a package the browser refused for exactly this

vectors.name: one label too few
vectors.because: a label per batting row, or a row has no name

vectors.name: an empty label
vectors.because: an empty string is not a position; it renders as a row with no name

vectors.name: a null footnote total
vectors.because: the client counted it as a blank and rendered no term for it, so the board could not be finished

vectors.name: a null batting total
vectors.because: that row IS erasable — the six reference packages all erase from it, which is why the two rows are not one rule

vectors.name: a malformed slot reference
vectors.because: the grammar is a slot with an optional letter; the client never checked it

vectors.name: a repeated slot reference
vectors.because: two rows answering to #1 makes a footnote attribution ambiguous, which is the field's whole purpose

vectors.name: metadata absent
vectors.because: seam C3 makes it loose in content, which is not the same as optional

vectors.name: metadata as an array
vectors.because: a list here breaks every reader that asks it for a key

vectors.name: offense_is_home absent
vectors.because: a board that cannot name its sides renders a false statement

vectors.name: offense_is_home as a number
vectors.because: 0 and 1 are the shape a producer in another language reaches for and they mean nothing here

vectors.name: schema 2
vectors.because: a v2 document has no offense_is_home and there is no honest default

vectors.name: a short batting row
vectors.because: a short row reads the next column's value into this one and every total still balances

vectors.name: a boolean cell
vectors.because: true is not a whole number, however truthy it is
